newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher, Suez, Lyonnaise soar.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher, Suez, Lyonnaise soar.

text.p: French shares climbed at the opening on Monday, with the market drawing support from the firm dollar and strong bond markets, traders said.
Some operators are factoring in a quarter percent rise in U.S. interest rates at Tuesday's Federal Reserve policy meeting.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 18.20 points or 0.70 percent at 2,605.33 at 0917 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 20 at 2,608. Volume was 500 million francs.
Utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux rises 2.67 percent to 576 francs, while holding company Suez up 2.4 percent at 287.10 following newspaper reports the two were preparing a merger.
Both declined comment on reports their chairmen wanted to hurry up merger talks ahead of Suez's April 1 board meeting.
"There must be something behind it," said a broker, who added that the market was waiting for merger details.

Utilities company Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) eased 0.4 percent to 744 francs. Financial weekly Investir reported CGE was preparing a counterattack on the rumoured merger and could even mount a hostile bid on Suez to thwart Lyonnaise.
But a source close to CGE said last Friday a takeover of Suez was not part of CGE's strategy of focusing on core businesses.

Since the arrival of Jean-Marie Messier as chairman, CGE has enjoyed the market's approval as he set out to clean up the balance sheet and explain strategy, while Lyonnaise has traded at a discount to the larger CGE.
Glass-maker Saint-Gobain rose 0.12 percent at 832. Le Monde reported its chairman Jean-Louis Beffa has been involved in the Suez/Lyonnaise merger talks.
On macroeconomic issues, a trader said even though people have priced in a U.S. rate rise, markets are still cautious and business would likely be subdued until the FOMC meeting was out of the way.
